memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the LORD said to Aaron, 'You and your sons are not to drink wine or other fermented drink whenever you go into the tent of meeting, or you will die. This is a lasting ordinance for the generations to come.'" - Lev 10:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice who speaks here. Throughout Leviticus, God has spoken to Moses. Now, for the first time, the LORD said to Aaron — directly, on the day he lost two sons.

God did not abandon Aaron in his grief. He came near and spoke to him personally.

The instruction concerns alcohol before ministry. Its placement immediately after Nadab and Abihu's death has led many to wonder whether drink was involved in their presumption. The text does not say so, and we should not claim more than Scripture does.

What is clear is the principle: the priests were to enter God's presence with clear minds and full attention.

Scripture does not forbid alcohol outright — Jesus made wine at Cana, and Paul told Timothy to take a little wine for his stomach (1 Tim 5:23). But it warns repeatedly against drunkenness and anything that clouds judgement in serious moments. Do not get drunk on wine, which leads to debauchery. Instead, be filled with the Spirit (Eph 5:18).

The deeper question is not only about drink. What dulls your attention when you come to God? What do you reach for that makes it harder to hear Him clearly?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What habits dull my attentiveness to God?
2. Do I come to God with a clear mind, or already half-distracted?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You spoke to Aaron personally in his grief. Clear away whatever dulls my attention to You. Amen.
